ambiguities: The narrator briefly frames himself as Albertine's 'époux et maître' whom she obeys, which could suggest a staged elevation of le narrateur; but he immediately disclaims this as a mistaken feeling of pride ('j'avais cru qu'il m'enorgueillissait. Je m'étais trompé.'), placing it at the level of retrospective self-analysis rather than a staged social interaction, so it was not scored.

Françoise repeatedly functions as the messenger/escort who transmits news of Albertine and brings her back, but the passage gives her no distinct evaluative treatment of her own (no praise of competence, no snub); her role is purely instrumental to the already-scored Albertine material, so she was omitted.
Gilberte appears only in a passing comparison ('depuis Gilberte et mes jeux aux Champs-Élysées') with no local evaluative content, so she was omitted.
